scope: upper-lip shell integration and commissure termination

experiments.method: Join the 325-vertex upper-lip shell to five surface-conforming transition rings; share the inner ring and bind the 650-vertex connected object to the evaluated body with Surface Deform.
experiments.normalFinding: 231 of 256 inherited shell faces pointed toward positive Y while all transition faces pointed outward. Reversing the inherited face winding removes the false dark outline.
experiments.cornerFade: A point-domain opacity ramp over five columns reduces the front needle but exposes a transparent layer and a vertical attachment edge obliquely.

experiments.method: Collapse all five shell rows toward one commissure position over eight columns and use a 0.20 mm body-transition clearance without alpha fading.
experiments.result: The needle shortens, but the separate lip shell still reads as a shelf and retains an oblique termination wall.

lockedToneEvidence.conclusion: No progressive skin darkening in the Blender mainline. Website working-tree GLB uses a different skin texture whose mean encoded luminance is 5.6% below the prior comparison GLB.

rejectionReasons: Upper lip remains visually detached from the orbicularis-oris region.
Commissures terminate as visible geometric walls in oblique view.
Surface Deform is an authoring dependency and has not been baked to engine-ready shape keys and skin weights.
Strict hero visual gate failed before promotion and full release collision/performance gates.
nextRequiredMethod: Replace the detached shell approach with continuous perioral edge rings following orbicularis-oris flow, including shared upper/lower commissure vertices, then transfer rig weights and rebuild expression shape keys before tint or microrelief work.
